name.text: Stationary points from the graph of the gradient

questiontext.text:
The graph shows the gradient function \(y = f'(x)\) of a curve \(y = f(x)\).

generalfeedback.text:
The stationary points of \(f\) are where \(f'(x) = 0\): where the graph of \(f'\) meets the \(x\)-axis, at \(x = {@s1@}\) and \(x = {@s2@}\). Where the graph of \(f'\) is above the axis, \(f\) is increasing; where it is below, \(f\) is decreasing.

\(x\)\(x \lt {@s1@}\)\({@s1@}\)\({@s1@} \lt x \lt {@s2@}\)\({@s2@}\)\(x \gt {@s2@}\)
Sign of \(f'(x)\)[[if test="is(ga>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]]\(0\)[[if test="is(gb>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]]\(0\)[[if test="is(gc>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]]
\(f\)[[if test="is(ga>0)"]]increasing[[else]]decreasing[[/if]]stationary[[if test="is(gb>0)"]]increasing[[else]]decreasing[[/if]]stationary[[if test="is(gc>0)"]]increasing[[else]]decreasing[[/if]]

So \(x = {@s1@}\) is a [[if test="is(n1=1)"]]maximum point[[elif test="is(n1=2)"]]minimum point[[else]]point of inflection[[/if]] and \(x = {@s2@}\) is a [[if test="is(n2=1)"]]maximum point[[elif test="is(n2=2)"]]minimum point[[else]]point of inflection[[/if]]. Where the graph of \(f'\) only touches the axis, \(f'\) does not change sign, so \(f\) does not turn.

truefeedback.text: That is where the gradient graph has its own turning point. The stationary points of \(f\) are where \(f'(x) = 0\), where the graph meets the \(x\)-axis.

falsefeedback.text: Read where the graph of \(f'\) meets the \(x\)-axis.

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(n1=1)"]]

You chose minimum point. Then \(f\) would be decreasing just before \(x = {@s1@}\) and increasing just after, so the graph of \(f'\) would pass from below the \(x\)-axis to above it there. Look at the graph on each side of \(x = {@s1@}\).

[[else]]

You chose maximum point. Then \(f\) would be increasing just before \(x = {@s1@}\) and decreasing just after, so the graph of \(f'\) would pass from above the \(x\)-axis to below it there. Look at the graph on each side of \(x = {@s1@}\).

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(n1=3)"]]

You chose minimum point. Then \(f\) would be decreasing just before \(x = {@s1@}\) and increasing just after, so the graph of \(f'\) would pass from below the \(x\)-axis to above it there. Look at the graph on each side of \(x = {@s1@}\).

[[else]]

You chose point of inflection. Then \(f'\) would have the same sign on both sides of \(x = {@s1@}\), so its graph would touch the \(x\)-axis there without crossing it. Look at the graph on each side of \(x = {@s1@}\).

[[/if]]
